Not every cheap power bank, camera or smart plug is just what the box says.

Some ship with:

→ their own cellular modem
→ their own SIM
→ firmware that phones home without ever touching your Wi-Fi

Your router never sees it.

So nothing ever looks wrong.

Here's the 2 minute check:

1. Plug it into a laptop with a data cable
2. Ask Claude Code: "list every USB device and interface this exposes"
3. A charger should show power only
4. Extra serial or network ports on a "battery" are a red flag

If you didn't buy it from a brand you trust, check it today.

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5 at once, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Better results and way fewer tokens, because every task lands on the right model.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session, writes the code and applies the fixes
→ Haiku 5.5 swarms the repo in parallel: search, grep and diff audits
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls and signs off on the diff
→ you stop burning Opus context on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku swarms. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and coordinates the work
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5, read-only
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5 in its own context
> audit checks the diff on Haiku 5.5 in a throwaway worktree
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reviews the synthesized diff before sign-off
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

• Its misses: talking heads, heavy edits
• It called live footage AI in 3 of 8

Experiment 2, full remake, ours vs REA-Video:
• SSIM: 0.96 vs 0.78

Bottom line:
• Simple UGC: both great
• Talking heads with motion graphics, B-roll and heavy editing, and launch videos with complex motion graphics: we do better
• REA-Video remakes slightly faster and cheaper

outsiders.text:
THIS IS AN ACTUAL F*CKING GOLDMINE

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5 at once, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Better results and way fewer tokens, because every task lands on the right model.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session, writes the code and applies the fixes
→ Haiku 5.5 swarms the repo in parallel: search, grep and diff audits
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls and signs off on the diff
→ you stop burning Opus context on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku swarms. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and coordinates the work
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5, read-only
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5 in its own context
> audit checks the diff on Haiku 5.5 in a throwaway worktree
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reviews the synthesized diff before sign-off
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Reconfigure my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three Haiku 5.5 subagents in .claude/agents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), audit (checks the diff).
3. Set isolation: worktree on audit so its checks never touch my working branch.
4. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: delegate every repo search and test run to the Haiku 5.5 subagents to keep the main context small.
5. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

claude code just got a much smarter workflow.

Anthropic has shown how to combine Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 so each model handles the work it's best at.

The goal? Get stronger reasoning when it matters without spending premium tokens on every small task.

Start Claude Code with:

"claude --model sonnet --advisor opus"

Here's how the team works:

→ Sonnet 5.5: Handles the main coding session and writes the code.

→ Haiku 5.5: Searches the repository, finds relevant functions and fetches documentation.

→ Opus 5.5: Acts as an independent advisor for important decisions.

Opus only steps in at three moments:

1. Before finalizing a plan.
2. When the same error happens twice.
3. Before marking a task complete.

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus thinks.

There's another layer: JEV handles simple decisions like tool selection, file paths and retries in milliseconds, leaving bigger models to focus on complex problems.

You can build this setup with three Haiku subagents, an Opus advisor and a few rules in CLAUDE.md.

Documentation: https://t.co/SnzyO1HzXA

Save this workflow. It's a smarter way to manage your Claude Code sessions and token usage.

Microsoft open-sourced an app that watches you do a task once, then teaches your AI agent to do it for you. 4.3K stars.

How Skill Recorder works:
1. Hit record (⌘⇧R or Ctrl+Shift+R) and do the task normally. You can talk through it out loud too.
2. It captures your clicks, app switches, pages and terminal commands, all on your machine.
3. GitHub Copilot turns the recording into a list of steps you can edit.
4. One click turns it into a skill your agent can run, or an automation on a schedule.

It generalizes from one example, so recording yourself submitting one form teaches the agent to submit all of them.
